items: Definition: Dependency Injection is a design pattern used to reduce tight coupling between software components. Instead of creating dependencies internally, objects receive their dependencies from an external source (like the Spring IoC Container).
Goal: Promotes loose coupling, easier testing, better maintainability, and modular design.
Definition: Wiring refers to the process of linking or injecting beans (objects) together in the Spring IoC Container using Dependency Injection.

content.text: Let’s look at a case where a Customer depends on a Plan.

items: Here, the Customer bean is manually wired with a Plan bean (specifically Prepaid).
This approach requires explicitly writing the dependency injection code in the configuration.

content.text: ⛔ Downside: Becomes cumbersome and verbose as the application grows.
Spring provides automatic wiring to inject dependencies without explicitly writing code.

rows: Injects bean by matching type of the property or parameter.
Used when multiple beans of the same type exist — uses bean name to resolve.
Injects dependency via setter method using @Autowired.

items: Plan bean will be injected directly into the Customer bean by type.
Must be a Spring-managed bean (@Component, @Service, etc.).
Spring automatically detects and calls the setter to inject Plan.
Ensures that the bean is created only if all required dependencies are provided.

content.text: When multiple beans of the same type exist, Spring needs help to pick the correct one. Qualifer is used to Disambiguate Dependencies

items: The bean names are the class names in lowercase by default ("prepaid", "postpaid").

sections.heading: Demo: Application Class to Run Autowiring

items: Wiring is the process of connecting beans using DI.
Manual wiring is explicit but tedious.
Use @Qualifier when multiple beans of the same type are present.
Prefer constructor injection for required dependencies.
Use setter or field injection for optional dependencies.
